title: Driver Quality Standards Bulletin: Driver Cancellation Rate and Acceptance Rate
content:
Every agreement under the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product is held to the cancellation standard of its Wayfare level. The level figures are in the cancellation standard schedule.

## Standard

1. **The rate.** The driver cancellation rate is driver cancellations over the most recent accepted trips of the level's rate window, leaving out the cancellations the schedule excludes.
2. **Recording.** Every breach is recorded as a cancellation warning on the standing record.
3. **Warning.** A rate above the level's cancellation rate threshold brings a cancellation warning.
4. **Hold.** A further breach while the level's number of cancellation warnings before a hold is on record within the warning validity days places the agreement on hold for the level's temporary hold length, after which the hold is lifted.
5. **Deactivation.** When the cancellation-rate breaches in the lookback reach the level's breaches for deactivation, the agreement is deactivated for cancellation rate instead of held. The breaches in the lookback are the cancellation-rate warnings on the agreement dated within the lookback days ending on the current day, inclusive; every cancellation-rate breach, whether it brought a warning or a hold, is recorded as one such warning.
6. **Acceptance rate.** The acceptance rate is never used for any warning, hold, level change or deactivation.

## Breach escalation (figures as on every level: 1 warning before a hold, 3 breaches for deactivation)

| Situation at a new breach | Result |
|---|---|
| no cancellation warning on record within the validity days, breaches in the lookback below 3 | cancellation warning |
| 1 cancellation warning on record within the validity days, breaches in the lookback below 3 | temporary hold for the level's hold days |
| breaches in the lookback reach 3 | deactivation for cancellation rate instead of a hold |

## Hypothetical example

A Wayfare XL driver (threshold 8.00 percent, hold of 3 days) has 100 accepted trips with 9 driver cancellations, one of them a rider no-show mark. The excluded cancellation leaves 8, a rate of 8.0 percent, which is not above 8.00, so there is no breach. With 10 driver cancellations of which one is excluded, the rate is 9.0 percent and is a breach.
